newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies, hogs tumble to lower closes.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies, hogs tumble to lower closes.

text.p: CME hog and pork belly futures tumbled to lower closes, a turnaround particularly in the hog pit from the new contract high posted in the December ahead of the slide, traders said.
February pork belly futures fell 3.000 cents from its early high of 79.850 cents to end 1.700 lower at 76.875 cents. Other belly contracts ended 1.825 to 0.075 cent lower.

Hogs finished 0.650 cent a lb lower to 0.100 higher with December closing 0.400 lower at 58.250 cents after setting a new contract high early of 58.950 cents. Lean December posted a new low of 62.200 cents.

Pork bellies climbed up to heavy technical resistance after starting lower, but turned down by midday and fell sharply late when commercial pressure and fund liquidation touched off sell stops. Futures went up to the projected high on this run and fell when reports circulated that the cash market may have also reached a short-term top, they said.
"The premium basis for the bellies maybe got too wide," said Dale Benson, vice president and senior livestock analyst with Dean Witter.
He noted the basis is now in line after the break and firm fundamentals may keep belly futures near current levels.
Hog slaughter has been light and movement of bacon has been very good recently, traders added.
R.J. O'Brien, Rosenthal Collins, Refco and Lind-Waldock sold on the setback in bellies, pit sources said.
Hog futures also pushed through initial profit taking and long liquidation to set a new high in December before retreating late on renewed commercial and fund selling, traders said.
Funds had been strong buyers on the runup to the new high but profit taking was again evident as the market looked overbought, especially with some cash weakness, traders said.
Cash pork sales slowed after recent advances and floor sources only cited steady price indications for cash hogs Tuesday despite recent tight hog marketings.
Rand Financials and Refco notably sold February late and were also early sellers. Merrill Lynch and Smith Barney also sold as R.J. O'Brien bought, pit sources said.
In hog options, traders were buying December 58 puts early on the rally in futures to lock in profits, traders said. E.D.& F. Man bought February 67 puts, pit sources added.
